complete_reset_preserve_erase_namespace_.detail: All 12 registry entries (components/service/include/nvs_namespace_registry.hpp), each with exactly one classification, matching FD-21's own preserve/erase text verbatim:

fd21_items_with_no_registry_entry.detail: Three FD-21 Preserve items are not NVS namespaces at all and so deliberately have no registry entry: eFuse/security state and Secure Boot/Flash/NVS encryption key material live in eFuse and the hardware-managed nvs_keys partition, not an app-owned NVS namespace; the factory GatewayId is derived at runtime from the eFuse-backed factory base MAC (hal_identity_get_factory_base_mac) and is never written to NVS at all. All three are preserved trivially, by construction.

complete_reset_preserve_erase_namespace_.enforcement: erase_namespace()/erase_namespace_key_range() (slice 10) refuse outright, before touching any key, for any namespace not classified kEraseOnFactoryReset -- this diff is not just documentation, it is structurally enforced.

what_this_stage_deliberately_did_not_do.no_production_call_site_migrated: network_manager.cpp, connectivity_manager.cpp, config_manager.cpp, matter_endpoint_registry.cpp and every other existing NVS consumer still call hal_nvs_* directly, completely unchanged from before S5 began. Nothing in this repository calls secure_storage_migrate_str(), erase_namespace(), erase_namespace_key_range(), or set_reset_journal_state(). This is intentional -- S5's job was to prove the foundation is real, correct and tested, not to wire it into production flows that themselves belong to S6 (authorization/physical-presence policy) and S8 (the actual factory-reset flow).
what_this_stage_deliberately_did_not_do.no_real_secret_material_generated: Every test across all eleven sub-slices uses only synthetic placeholder bytes (0xA1/0xB2-style filler, 'hunter2'/'MyNetwork' as test strings) -- directly satisfying plan #13's 'this stage does not generate untracked production certificates or shared secrets' and plan #8's 'never place production private keys in the repository'. Confirmed via a direct grep audit (slice 9) of this repository's own implementation-evidence/*.json and docs/security/*.md files: zero matches for PEM markers, password-shaped patterns, or the specific synthetic test values used.

unresolved_deviations_carried_forward: Real per-category ESP-IDF NVS namespace routing does not exist -- hal_nvs.c still hardcodes a single 'zigbee_gateway' namespace for every key. Slice 7's same-key-migration-rejection finding confirms this matters concretely for any real migration, not just in the abstract.

dependencies.lock's own git-tracked 'idf: version: 5.5.2' pin disagrees with the real toolchain (5.5.5) this project's CI actually uses -- found in slice 3, deliberately not edited (a separate, reviewable change).

No CI job builds the production profile through the real ESP-IDF container on every push/PR yet -- now much lower-risk to add, since this stage repeatedly proved a full production build succeeds end-to-end (11 separate real-target build verifications across the eleven sub-slices, two of which caught and fixed real bugs).

Whether/when to enable coredump-to-flash is an open, unrelated product decision (slice 9) -- the reserved partition predates S5, nothing currently turns the feature on, and CONFIG_ESP_COREDUMP_CAPTURE_DRAM is now forbidden regardless of that decision's outcome.
The concrete key names this stage invented for kTlsIdentity/kManufacturingProvisioning (slice 8) are not derived from any real S6 design (none exists yet) and may need to change once one does.

erase_namespace() does not automatically discover or apply prefix-key erase ranges for kZigbeeNetworkDeviceReporting -- a caller must supply erase_namespace_key_range()'s parameters explicitly, as this stage's own tests do for the one real case (slice 10).
unresolved_blockers: No manufacturing/eFuse environment or physical ESP32-C6 hardware available anywhere in this sandbox -- BLOCKED_SECURITY_PROVISIONING, per plan S5's own precondition text ('if irreversible provisioning cannot be dry-run and read back, return BLOCKED_SECURITY_PROVISIONING'). This blocks exactly plan #6, #7 and #8's burn-time-enforcement half, plus every target/HIL test in S5's own test list. Every other required change in this stage -- all of #1-#5, #9-#18, and #8's non-hardware half -- is complete, tested, and (wherever a new real ESP-IDF Kconfig symbol or API was introduced) verified against the real ESP-IDF toolchain, not just the host build.
